statement: For finite F′/K(μ∞), abelian torsion is finite, Tate invariants and torus-to-abelian Tate homomorphisms vanish, abelian divisible points vanish, and divisible units are exactly μ∞.
notes: Number-field descent and cocycle proofs are written out; no Mordell–Weil assumption needed for Kummer injectivity.

statement: For affine hyperbolic curves, distinct lifted cusp inertia groups have trivial intersection; Nπ(Ic)=Ic and Cπ(z)=Ic for 1≠z∈Ic; the arithmetic normalizer of any nontrivial closed J⊂Ic is Dc; the boundary abelianization sequence is exact.
The all-N boundary-image criterion recognizes inertia elements; comparison with Nakamura(2.1.1)–(2.1.4), Stix2008 Theorem20 and 2012 Theorem30 is explicit.
depends_on: A2; Nakamura1994 §2.1; Stix2008 Theorem20; Stix2012 Theorem30
notes: Author2012 manuscript opened; publisher PDF access blocked; numbering cross-check limited to author version.

statement: R2 steps1–3: proper cyclotomic centralizers vanish; every nonidentity affine centralizer element is inertia and fixes its cusp.
A closed subgroup consisting entirely of inertia elements lies in one inertia subgroup; direct two-product proof repairs R2 step4.
notes: Finite derangement and boundary checks run; code/A_boundary_checks.py and .out.

statement: For a number-field hyperbolic curve, the cyclotomic-kernel centralizer is nontrivial exactly for a cuspidal section and then equals its unique inertia group.
notes: Two complete routes: direct geometric lemma and verified Stix hypothesis over F.

statement: Germs and open subgroups of Γ° have the same inertia centralizer; larger closed subgroups give exactly the product of cyclotomically trivial ℓ-components.

Explicit centralizers for the exceptional types: proper genus1 and types(0,0),(0,1) give1; split type(0,2) gives the whole geometric group for every section. Over R the cyclotomic kernel is trivial and every section has the entire geometric group as centralizer; real-place restriction maps are specified.
notes: The real C2 character is checked modulo4; number-field conclusions retain their stated arithmetic hypotheses.

statement: Specialization proves finite torsion over cyclotomic extensions of finitely generated characteristic-zero fields; all required Tate/divisibility and centralizer consequences extend.
Corrected H1: every nonzero centralizer is a unique cusp inertia fixed subgroup; normal Δ gives cuspidality, including uniqueness of a fixed cusp with zero centralizer.
notes: For arbitrary nonnormal Δ with no trivial cyclotomic component, uniqueness of fixed cusps is not claimed; exact remaining assertion is stated.

statement: H1 holds for single/all cyclotomic towers and radical extensions covered by Murotani–Ozeki; for K^ab it holds exactly when K contains no CM subfield.
Original H1 is false: over Q with a tangential section at0 and Δ=G_Q(μ_3∞), its Tate hypothesis holds, χ|Δ is nontrivial, and the centralizer is Z3(1).
notes: The strongest proved replacement is AE2: componentwise fixed inertia; no finite computer calculation is substituted for the infinite cyclotomic argument.
